questions.title: How many people can each room hold, by the code?
questions.why: Occupant load is floor area divided by the code's load factor. The area comes from the drawn room, the factor from the clause, both kept as data, so changing either recomputes the floor. Rooms over 49 need a second exit (question E3).

questions.title: How far is each room from its nearest open exit?
questions.why: Distance along the corridor and into the room (x plus z, from the scene) to each open exit door; whether a stair is open, from the record. A code review measures the true walking path, so this is a screening number, not a finding.

questions.title: Does every room over 49 people have two ways out?
questions.why: Counting doors is a record question (BOT interfaces); which rooms need two is a scene question (area). The room lights green when it has them.

inference.title: Every space that can reach Exit stair A
inference.why: BOT says which spaces each door joins. A rule turns doors into connections, and the path query lights everything that can reach the stair.

fault_text: Door 402 is drawn 0.76 m (30 in) wide, and the record says Exit stair B is locked.
